newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IMF mission to Romania ahead of board meeting.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission to Romania ahead of board meeting.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund mission is to visit Romania next week ahead of a Fund meeting on resuming credits to back the new centrist government's reforms, an IMF statement said on Friday.

The statement issued by Fund representative John Hill said the mission was routine in nature to monitor the progress of the government's reform programme drafted in February with the help of the IMF and other Western institutions.
"This is a routine visit to examine day-by-day progress," Hill said by telephone.
He said the government had prepared a standard letter of intent in connection with the programme of credits, to be discussed at an IMF Executive Board meeting in Washington on April 23 and 24.
He described Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's reform programme as "bold and comprehensive".
The IMF suspended credits to Romania last year, complaining that the leftist government, ousted in last November's elections, had overshot spending targets and hobbled foreign exchange markets.
Talks on putting together a new aid package were launched in January and government sources have suggested that a total of $400 million will eventually be on offer.

Ciorbea has repeatedly said there can be no alternatives to the reforms after seven years of what Romanian and Western experts agree was timid change after the 1989 overthrow of Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
The new programme has already introduced steep price increases on staples and utilities and calls for cuts in spending and state subsidies.
Monthly inflation, which stood at 18.8 percent in February is to be reduced to 2.2 percent by the end of the year.
The budget deficit is to be trimmed to 4.5 percent from last year's figure of 5.8 percent -- nearly three times higher than government targets.
